newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Enterprises IPO generates strong interest.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Enterprises IPO generates strong interest.

text.p: The start of Beijing Enterprises Holdings Co Ltd's initial public offering (IPO) generated unusually strong interest among small investors in Hong Kong on Tuesday, brokers said.
They said that the underwriting banks had run out of application forms for potential purchasers to subscribe to the IPO, which was unusual on the first day of an offering.
Peregrine Capital Ltd, one of the global coordinators of the issue, was set to print more forms to meet the strong demand, a source close to Peregrine said.
Beijing Enterprises is the latest IPO of a China-backed red chip stock which Hong Kong investors hope will deliver strong price appreciation.

"I would not be surprised if there is also a grey market price for the application form as people are crazy for the stock in anticipation of strong capital gains," said one sales manager at a regional brokerage.

Beijing Enterprises, which is controlled by the Beijing municipal government, is offering 150 million shares in a global flotation at HK$12.48 per share. Of the total, 10 percent are being offered to the Hong Kong public and 90 percent designated for international placement.
The deadline for applications to subscribe is on Friday. Dealing in the company shares is expected to begin on May 29.

Analysts said investors were hoping for a repeat of the reception given Shanghai Industrial Investment (Holdings) Co Ltd which was offered last year and saw its price rise more than five times above its issue price over 12 months.
The grey market price of Beijing Enterprises was about HK$37 on Tuesday, analysts said.
Beijing Enterprises is the primary commercial vehicle for the Beijing municipal government to access international markets for capital, technology and management expertise.
The company is a conglomerate involved in retailing, infrastructure, hotel services and the high-tech industry.
Analysts said the company's close link with its Beijing parent should give it access to high quality projects.
"It gives people a rare opportunity of participating in the fast growing city of Beijing," said Hugo So, analyst at Yamaichi International.
Peregrine Capital and Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd are the joint global coordinators of the issue.

Analysts said the strong interest among retail investors was helped by news earlier that seven major firms, including several Hong Kong blue chips, had agreed to subscribe to a total of 36 million shares, or six percent of the enlarged share capital.
